reading:
Prime Data Centers was founded in 2017 in California by Nicholas Laag, who remains Founder and CEO of the majority founder-owned private company, now headquartered at 400 North Ervay Street in Dallas, Texas.

The company's own site describes 28 facilities across 13 campuses, spanning North American markets in Austin, Chicago, Dallas, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Sacramento, and Silicon Valley, plus EMEA campuses in Frankfurt, Germany and Madrid, Spain, with planned expansion into Esbjerg, Denmark. Prime states a more than 4 gigawatt expansion pipeline, with individual facilities ranging from 3 to 12 megawatts for a single data hall up to 100 or more megawatts for a full campus. Named projects include a 240 megawatt campus in Phoenix, Arizona and a 160 megawatt initial phase in Denmark with planned expansion to 550 megawatts.

The registry here tracks 5 Prime facilities across two states, California and Texas, a subset of the company's seven named North American markets, which also include Austin, Chicago, Los Angeles, Phoenix, and Sacramento. Prime's stated 240 megawatt Phoenix campus is a useful figure to cross-check against this registry's Arizona facility rows during the facility-level research phase, alongside the Phoenix-area capacity already recorded for NTT elsewhere in this registry.
